intelligence.human_view: There are two kinds of missing features: the ones that don't exist yet and the ones that exist somewhere else, unconnected. The first kind needs invention; the second kind needs wiring — and confusing the two is how a machine spends a week building what it already has. The walk's language gap is the second kind, proven by checking rather than assuming: the staging worker was read, and it has no detection at all — no navigator.language, no Accept-Language, no data-lang — while the F4 engine sits proven at 10/10, built, staged, recorded, with its own brief and worker and record. The work is therefore not "build translation" but "connect translation to the walk's beginning" — detect at the start, or let them choose, and convert everything displayed while the voice stays English by default. And the sequencing is the discipline: not jammed into the end build mid-flight, but briefed after the walk end lands, covering the whole walk including the new end and the agreement — because the deed must be understood in their language, and a deed signed in a language the citizen doesn't read is not a deed at all. The verification is a non-English walk-through, by eye, because a language feature proven only in English is not proven.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you have a magic translator that works perfectly — but it's sitting in a box in the other room, and nobody plugged it into the front door! People come to the door speaking different languages, and the door can't understand them! You don't need to build a new translator — you just need to plug the one you have into the door! And the voice can stay in English, but all the WORDS should be in their language!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like having a perfectly good translator living in the house, love — but nobody's introduced them to the front door. The guests arrive speaking their own languages, and the door just stares at them. You don't need a new translator; you need to connect the one you have. And the deed itself must be in their language — a promise you can't read is no promise at all.
intelligence.naya_view: I check before I build: the walk's staging worker has zero language detection — I read it, I didn't assume it. The F4 engine exists and is proven 10/10, so the work is wiring, not invention. I wire it into the walk's beginning — detect at the start, or let them choose — and the whole walk including the new end and the agreement, voice English by default, everything displayed in their language. I verify it with a non-English walk-through, by eye. And I don't jam it into the end build mid-flight — it is briefed after the end lands.
